meta.doctrine: Patterns move HYPOTHESIS → ACTIVE → STRESSED → CONFIRMED or BROKEN. A CONFIRMED pattern is load-bearing for analysis; a BROKEN pattern must never be silently reused. Every state change carries the evidence that caused it.

patterns.name: IRGC overrides the diplomatic track
patterns.rule: Trust Khamenei Telegram for operational intent; treat Araghchi/MFA as diplomatic narrative only.
patterns.evidence: IRGC publicly overrode the FM since Apr 2026 (UK Commons Library). Escalated 8 Jul: Witkoff and Kushner told Trump that Araghchi could not guarantee the IRGC would stop firing on shipping — and the renewed US strikes followed directly from that report (Israel Hayom). The split is no longer just an Iran-reading problem; it now drives US targeting decisions.

history.note: IRGC publicly contradicts FM on Hormuz
UK Commons Library confirms Mojtaba-Pezeshkian divergence on MOU
Split becomes a US casus belli via Witkoff/Kushner report

patterns.name: Iran signals before acting
patterns.rule: Assume Iranian kinetic action can come with zero prior signal. Absence of warning is not absence of intent.
patterns.evidence: Broken 18 Apr (IRGC fired without VHF warning). Re-validated 11 Jul: the GFS Galaxy was hit and disabled with a crew member missing — and Iran itself styled the strike a ‘warning shot.’ The warning IS the strike now.

history.note: VHF warnings preceded interceptions
Fire without warning
GFS Galaxy: the ‘warning shot’ disables the ship

patterns.name: Lebanon drives Hormuz re-closures
patterns.rule: Check the Lebanon front on every Hormuz event — but no longer assume it is the only driver.
patterns.evidence: Every re-closure through June traced to Lebanon (it is MOU Point 1). The 11 Jul closure declaration broke the chain: it traced to route enforcement (GFS Galaxy / southern-lane jurisdiction), not Lebanon. The Israel-Hezbollah ceasefire (19 Jun) is holding but fragile — Israel refuses withdrawal (Katz: security zones ‘for an unlimited period’). Downgraded CONFIRMED → STRESSED: the route war is now an independent closure driver.

history.note: Two re-closures trace to Lebanon
MOU makes Lebanon Point 1
First closure NOT traced to Lebanon — route enforcement instead

patterns.name: Trump maximal rhetoric, preserved off-ramp
patterns.rule: Never read Trump’s rhetoric as policy. Read the delegation manifest instead.
patterns.evidence: Upgraded ACTIVE → CONFIRMED 11 Jul on the cleanest instance yet: within hours of ‘1000 missiles locked and loaded’ and declaring the MOU dead, the most senior US team of the war (Vance, Rubio, Witkoff, Kushner) was dispatched toward Muscat. Re-validated 13-14 Jul in the economic domain: the ‘Guardian of the Strait’ 20% toll was announced and abandoned within ~24 hours while the operational policy (blockade + escorts) never wavered. The rhetoric and the off-ramp are the same policy; read the operations, not the announcements.

history.note: ‘It’s over’ / ‘scum’ while talks continue
Ceasefire ‘over’ at NATO; talks not terminated
Decimation threats + most senior delegation of the war, same day
20% toll floated and dropped in ~24h; blockade policy unchanged throughout

patterns.name: Iran floats maximal options, executes calibrated ones
patterns.rule: Stated options (NPT, Bab-el-Mandeb) are bargaining inventory, not warning orders — but the calibration ceiling is rising.
patterns.evidence: Held in form on 11 Jul: NPT withdrawal and Bab-el-Mandeb (floated 8 Jul) stayed unexecuted; Iran instead closed its own strait — the maximal option fully inside its control. Marked STRESSED because ‘calibrated’ now includes a formal closure declaration. New form 16 Jul: Bab el-Mandeb returns not as a float but as a reported CONDITIONAL order to the Houthis with a trigger (strikes on Iranian power infrastructure) that has since been met. A conditional order with a satisfied trigger is a different object from a float — it pre-commits, shifts execution to a proxy, and lets Iran deny agency. Watch execution, not restatement.

history.note: Bab-el-Mandeb threatened repeatedly, never executed
NPT + Bab-el-Mandeb floated as options
Executed option (closure) is itself near-maximal
Bab el-Mandeb re-emerges as a conditional proxy order; trigger condition met, unexecuted so far

patterns.name: Israel re-enters when US-Iran talks stall
patterns.rule: The stall-trigger framing is weakening — replace with the two-condition frame: Israel re-enters on a direct Iranian attack or a US request. Israeli-official leaks during negotiations are still pressure instruments.
patterns.evidence: New 11 Jul: Ynet and ToI report Israel preparing to rejoin as talks stall — all Israeli-official sourcing. Counter-evidence 13-16 Jul: the talks didn't just stall, they collapsed entirely, and through six subsequent strike nights Israel STILL did not enter. Israeli officials now state the two conditions explicitly (direct attack or US request), and Israeli assessments say Iran is deliberately avoiding drawing the IDF in. The hypothesis as originally stated (stall → entry) failed its cleanest test; what remains is the two-condition frame plus Iranian targeting discipline as the active variable.

history.note: First explicit re-entry signalling since the MOU
Stall-trigger version failed (total collapse, no entry); reframed to the two-condition trip-wires

patterns.name: Strikes and talks run as parallel tracks, not alternatives
patterns.rule: Grade the kinetic and diplomatic tracks separately — but do not assume the diplomatic track is durable. It can break while the kinetic one accelerates.
patterns.evidence: Proposed 12 Jul (three strike rounds + senior delegations at once). Stressed 13 Jul: the tracks diverged rather than ran parallel — Round 4 on the same day the Muscat talks collapsed. Held at STRESSED (not BROKEN) 17 Jul on a technicality with teeth: four days with zero formal sessions against six strike nights means there is currently only ONE track — but the channel's principals still meet (White House, 15 Jul) and Vance still publicly owns the MOU trajectory ('right… just really messy'). The pattern survives only if a venue reappears; the 17 Jul scenario set already refuses to lean on it (explicit haircut per ledger lesson).

history.note: Three strike rounds + senior delegations in the same week
Round 4 accelerates as Muscat talks collapse — tracks diverge, not parallel
Four days, zero sessions, six strike nights — one track running; BROKEN if no venue by ~24 Jul

patterns.name: Iran deliberately exempts the UAE from retaliation rounds
patterns.rule: REFINED: the exemption covers UAE TERRITORY, not UAE assets or interests. UAE quiet ≠ UAE safe. Track the exemption itself as a signal: its end would mark a strategic decision, not an accident.
patterns.evidence: New 12 Jul: Iran struck four states but not the UAE, the war’s most-targeted state pre-MOU. The improved gather (13 Jul re-run) forced a split definition: Iranian cruise missiles struck the UAE tankers al-Bahiya and Mombasa on 13 Jul, killing a crew member — and the UAE issued its first missile alert in months on 12 Jul (threats intercepted before entering its airspace). So UAE soil is exempt (day 10 and holding through six rounds), UAE assets are not. The Kuwait desalination strike (17 Jul) further narrows what the exemption is worth: GCC civilian utilities are now a demonstrated target class. Possible drivers unchanged: reconstruction-fund economics, Abu Dhabi back-channel, target saturation. Watch UAE MOD/WAM/NCEMA language for the first crack.

history.note: Four states hit this round; UAE conspicuously excluded
UAE tankers struck (1 killed) while UAE soil stays untouched — exemption narrows to territory
Day 10 of territorial exemption; Kuwait utility strike puts GCC infrastructure in the target class

patterns.name: Infrastructure strikes are answered in kind, category for category
patterns.rule: When one side widens the target set to a new infrastructure category, expect the other to answer in the same category within ~48h — on whatever territory it can reach. Watch the category, not the geography.
patterns.evidence: Proposed 17 Jul on one clean sequence: US night-six strikes hit southern Iran's civilian infrastructure (bridges, airports, power, rail — days after Trump publicly threatened Iranian infrastructure); within ~24h Iran struck Kuwait's power-and-desalination station, its first GCC civilian-infrastructure target of the war. One instance = hypothesis only. Test: does the next US infrastructure category (ports? refineries?) produce a matching Iranian answer in the GCC? Confirmation would make every US target-set decision a direct predictor of GCC civilian risk — the single most UAE-relevant pattern on the board if it holds.

history.note: Proposed: US infra strikes (night 6) answered by Kuwait desalination hit within ~24h
